logline: Resurrecting Atlantis is the arrival: winged marble gates open, a drowned city rises from black water, and a candlelit city of narrow streets takes him in, while the last line admits it was built out of 'the purest of fictions'.
reading:
One long sentence carries him from the gates ('wings gifted from evolution', marble 'kissed by the hymns' of an orchestra of ancestors' dreams) down 'yellow brick roads', which make Oz's road to a made city explicit, following comets 'to the capital city of our collective consciousness.' Then comes the creed, said twice as if learned by heart: 'Here we are all one... here we are all safe', the pact made with nature, 'a relearned currency we reassess' as the price of admission. The repetition is the poem's music and its doubt. It sounds like a vow being rehearsed.

The turn is 'I know my soul and it could stay here forever, leaving behind crosshairs for continuums and strains for serendipity': the targeted body trades the gunsight for continuity. The last line both confirms and undoes the city: 'A city born in unison out of the purest of fictions welcoming me and welcoming all.' The governing images are gate wings and marble, comets over a road, flickering candlelight on smiles, narrow streets with long shadows, joyful noise that colours rainbows and sets clouds free, and the crosshair opening into rings.
motifs: a gate with wings: marble, hymns, an orchestra of ancestors
the yellow-brick road / causeway, following comets
the creed said twice: here we are all one, here we are all safe
a relearned currency paid at admission (the coin)
flickering candlelight on smiles at night
narrow streets, long shadows, joyful noise turning to rainbows
a city of fiction, welcoming me and welcoming all

light_and_texture: It is night throughout, and the city lights itself from inside. Gold reflections on black water are foil and cellophane strips on gloss-black card; neon is cut acetate gel backlit; candles are small amber paper flames on a flicker. Buildings are white card with grey gouache veining and a pearl wash, stacked in 4-5 depths with windows punched through and backlit, and fog is tracing paper. Keep the cyberpunk sheen in the plates and the cut-outs matte kraft, so the people always read warmer than the city.

fx.how: Paper comet cards with long tissue tails pulled on a diagonal track; the tail tears off softly at the end.
A small amber paper disc lifts from a traveller's chest on a wire, then follows a comet's path.
A cut star-flare card pops on the dome tip for 6 frames, then decays to a steady point.
A blue cellophane water card pulled down in front of the city; water streaming is a stack of white paper drips sliding on loops.
Foil and gel strips on gloss-black card under each light, rippled with a slow displacement.
Acetate gel shapes backlit, with a 1-frame flicker every few seconds.
Swap among three flame cards at random 2-4 frame intervals; the warm gradient on faces breathes with them.
Project the Our Community (1952) dappled-shadow archive across the wall cards; cast hard puppet shadows at a low angle.
Prism stripes (code) thrown from the guitar's sound hole across the wall and onto his face card, pulsing with the strum.
Grey tissue clouds tethered between roofs by threads; the threads snap and the clouds drift up and out.
Code-drawn reticle over the plaza; its arms break into squares that fly outward and settle as concentric kraft rings, echoing the iris in gen_9f26db2b7a.
A grid of window cut-outs lit by a sweep from centre outward in one second; dome beacon last.
A warm polygon of light on the step and street that pulses lightly; coloured flecks drift out of the doorway.

passage.keep: 'Purest of fictions' is the right line: the poem admits the city is made just as he reaches a real door. A hand that stops short is one held gesture, and an open doorway is a tall, bright, vertical surface, the strongest kind. The Belmont Woman's Club tour ('the spout had to be facing the door as a sign of welcoming') is warm daylight interior film, so it will read inside a night frame.
passage.better: Build the door as a near-layer card frame so the archive fills a large pane, not a small far one. Keep the street plate figure-free and move the entering guests to cut-out party_guest cards passing behind the frame edge. Use the profile head and a dedicated 'reach-stopping-short' hand card; let the music light spill on his hand and stop at the same gap. If P06-011 has generated figures at the door, crop to gen_9c5f9c7c4a's doorway instead.
alt_lines: 06_L09 'An unfamiliar flickering candlelight illuminating smiles': object held out, a citizen offers a candle across the counter; the arched lantern-window in the gate wall opens on home-movie faces by candlelight (birthday or vigil archive).

06_L12 'leaving behind crosshairs for continuums': fist at the chest opens into a flat palm (one held change); a lit shopfront pane (gen_ec59e580b9) opens on a training-film gunsight that the code turns into ripples.

06_L01 'The gates open with wings gifted from evolution': palm on the marble leaf as it opens; the widening seam between the wings opens on Invitation to a Nation (1946, arch_2e67f50d), the dome framed in an arch.
06_L05 'Here we are all one': arms open and held at the waterline; a tower's lit window band clearing the water opens on archive of a crowd joining hands (dance, church, march).

ideas: Causeway in layers: four receding brick trapezoids on gloss-black card, view_035's spires sunk to the tips, and the ELDER's lantern glass playing How Man Made Day (arch_be3bace2) as the flame. The lantern is the archive.

The waterline falls: a blue cellophane sheet slides down in front of gen_69ee5bb28b's marble city while paper drips loop off the ledges. On the dome, one bright window band shows a 1939 World's Fair illuminated tower.
Admission: the coin card sets down on the booth counter and the booth glass shows a brief archive of ticket-takers and turnstiles. The coin glows, the neon rim goes pink and the queue moves.
Candle windows: two arched cut-outs shaped after This Is Russia (arch_d4664dde) hold citizen head cards that swap calm→joy as candle flames (arch_aef90d78) rise into frame.

Narrow street track: view_062 as plate, the puppet on a rail, Our Community (1952) shadows sliding across the walls, string-light card overhead. Over the cut to the musician alcove (view_061), prism light hits the wall.
Crosshairs to continuums: a reticle over view_033's round plaza; its arms shatter into rings that match gen_9f26db2b7a's iris, then a cut to the puppet's braced head swapping to lifted.
Clouds set free: tissue clouds tethered between roof cards snap loose into Sunburst (arch_5e2737d2) light. 'Infinite time to heal' is held on that shot.
The door: the near-layer red frame over gen_9c5f9c7c4a, with the corridor lamps of the Custom House film (arch_7c142971) as the interior seen past the guests before the Belmont answer plays.
